children: Adobe's fiscal third-quarter earnings were robust, but the software group's focus on attracting more customers weighs on its near-term outlook, JPMorgan analysts write. The company is happy to put monetization on the back burner in order to focus on expanding its pool of users with the aim that some will convert into paying customer, the analysts write. "Investors will look for proof points in relation to engagement turning into monetization," they say.There are signs that increased user engagement is translating into revenue, with annual recurring revenue in the group's Firefly app and credit pack growing by 40% on quarter, the analysts say. Adobe shares fall 3.1% premarket. (josephmichael.stonor@wsj.com)
